references.text: Jesus himself explains that this woman had been bound by Satan for eighteen years. [ref:Luk 13:16|Luke 13:16] gives the spiritual explanation for her condition – she had a spirit of infirmity that kept her bound.

In [ref:Luk 4:33-35|Luke 4:33-35], Jesus drives out an unclean spirit in the synagogue. Also here in Luke 13:11, it is an evil spirit causing sickness – a recurring theme in Luke where illness is linked to demonic activity.

[ref:Luk 8:2|Luke 8:2] mentions women who had been healed of evil spirits and diseases, including Mary Magdalene. This shows the connection between evil spirits and physical illness, as with the woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years.
[ref:Apg 10:38|Acts 10:38] summarizes Jesus' ministry: he healed all who were oppressed by the devil. The woman in Luke 13:11 is a clear example of this – bound by Satan with a spirit of infirmity.
In [ref:Job 2:7|Job 2:7], Satan strikes Job with sores. This is a parallel to Luke 13:11 where an evil spirit causes physical suffering – Satan is given permission to afflict people with disease.

The number eighteen is also mentioned in [ref:Luk 13:4|Luke 13:4] regarding the eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam fell. Luke uses this number twice in the same chapter, both times in connection with suffering and the question of God's will.

The psalmist in [ref:Sal 38:7|Psalm 38:7] describes himself as completely bowed down and hunchbacked – "I walk bent and crooked all day long." This recalls the woman's condition in Luke 13:11, where she was bent over and could not straighten herself.

[ref:Sal 146:8|Psalm 146:8] says that "the Lord lifts up those who are bowed down." The woman in Luke 13:11 was literally bowed down and was lifted up by Jesus – a fulfillment of this promise of God's care for the suffering.

[ref:Heb 7:25|Hebrews 7:25] says that Jesus is able to save "completely" (εἰς τὸ παντελές). The same expression is used in Luke 13:11 about how the woman could not straighten herself "completely." The linguistic parallel is striking.
